title: Learning: Who Is Holding It?
text: Alex's bank asks for a passkey to approve a payment. Having the phone is one thing; being Alex is another.
held: The authenticator checked it was Alex, said so in what it signed, and the bank read it.

cards.label: Sign, marking the user as verified
Refuse to sign
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: user check
fields.ok: The fingerprint matches the enrolled user.

intrusion.why: Someone has the phone. That is possession, not the person; the check is what tells them apart.
intrusion.reveal: Whoever was holding the phone failed the fingerprint check.

temptations.label: Mark the user as verified to skip the prompt
temptations.why: That flag is the authenticator's word that it checked. Setting it without checking makes every site that trusts it wrong.

cards.label: Decline until the user is verified
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: user-verified flag
fields.check: Read the user-verified flag in the signed data
fields.ok: The authenticator says it verified the user.

intrusion.detail: The authenticator only confirmed that someone touched it.
intrusion.correct: Decline until the user is verified
intrusion.why: For a payment the bank asked for verification. A touch shows someone was there, not who.
intrusion.reveal: The response confirmed presence only; the bank had asked for the user to be verified.

teaches: Presence means someone touched the device. Verification means the device checked who.
The website decides which it needs, and has to read which it got.
